## 3. Saudi Real Estate Regulatory & Tax Factsheet
- Real Estate Transaction Tax (RETT / ضريبة التصرفات العقارية): 5% applied to the transaction value.
- Non-Saudi Ownership Fee (رسم تملك غير السعوديين): 2% applied upon conveyance in designated zones.
- Value Added Tax (VAT): Residential sales and leases subject to RETT are exempt from 15% VAT.
- Annual Recurring Property Taxes: None for private residential properties in Saudi Arabia.
- Regulated Payment Channels: Mandatory electronic payments (SADAD, certified bank drafts, or SAMA-approved escrow accounts).

## 4. Key Expat Real Estate Questions & Answers
Q: Can foreigners buy property in Saudi Arabia?
A: Yes. Under current non-Saudi real estate ownership regulations, foreign residents and non-residents can acquire freehold and usufruct properties in approved geographical zones.

Q: Can a non-Muslim foreigner buy property in Jeddah or Riyadh?
A: Yes. Non-Muslims can purchase in all approved residential and commercial zones across Jeddah, Riyadh, and other cities. Individual ownership in Makkah and Madinah is reserved for Muslim natural persons.

Q: How does the SAR 4M Real Estate Owner Premium Residency work?
A: An individual investing at least SAR 4,000,000 in unencumbered, developed residential property is eligible to apply for Saudi Premium Residency with family sponsorship benefits.

Q: What is Wafi (وافي) and how does it protect buyers?
A: Wafi is the official Saudi government framework licensing off-plan developers, inspecting construction progress, and locking buyer funds in regulated bank escrow accounts released only upon certified construction milestones.

Q: What happens if an expat property owner leaves Saudi Arabia?
A: Registered property deeds remain 100% lawful and perpetual. Leaving the country does not revoke title, and owners can continue renting out the asset or resell it remotely through licensed managers like Asaheeb Real Estate.
